arxiv-2108-06601.description: Abstract Constitutive functions that govern macroscale capillary pressure and relative permeability are central in constraining both storage efficiency and sealing properties of CO 2 {}_{\textrm{2}} storage systems. Constitutive functions for porous systems are in part determined by wettability, which is a pore-scale phenomenon that influences macroscale displacement.

arxiv-2203-07534.creator: Luther Rinehart
arxiv-2203-07534.description: Abstract We show that a second-order elliptic differential operator P P , on any manifold M M , has closed range in C ∞ ​ ( M ) C^{\infty}(M) . If M M has no compact components, then P P is surjective on C ∞ ​ ( M ) C^{\infty}(M) . Applications to Helmholtz decomposition are discussed.

arxiv-2506-01105.title: A Positivity-Preserving Finite Element Framework for Accurate Dose Computation in Proton Therapy
arxiv-2506-01105.creator: Ben S. Ashby, Abdalaziz Hamdan, Tristan Pryer
arxiv-2506-01105.description: Abstract . We present a stabilised finite element method for modelling proton transport in tissue, incorporating both inelastic energy loss and elastic angular scattering. A key innovation is a positivity-preserving formulation that guarantees non-negative fluence and dose, even on coarse meshes. This enables reliable computation of clinically relevant quantities for treatment planning.

pmc-10623759.title: Efficacy and safety of venetoclax in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: a meta-analysis
pmc-10623759.creator: Xiaohui Gao, Hui Zeng, Xiaoyan Zhao, Haibing Wu, Minchao Yan, Yuan Li, Gang Zhang, Fei Sun
pmc-10623759.description: BackgroundVenetoclax is clinically active in treating relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of venetoclax or venetoclax with other agents in treating RRMM.MethodsPubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library were comprehensively searched. We included studies investigating the efficacy and safety of venetoclax or venetoclax with other agents in treating RRMM.

pmc-10772769.title: Factors Influencing Tobacco Cessation in India: Findings from the Global Adult Tobacco Survey-2
pmc-10772769.creator: GK Mini, Radhakrishnan Jayakrishnan, Krishna Kumar Jishnu, K Kumar Anil
pmc-10772769.description: Objective:The study aimed to assess the socio-demographic and other correlates of cessation behavior across tobacco products among the adult population in India. Methods:We used data of adults (aged ≥15 years) who were current or former tobacco users (smoking and/or smokeless tobacco) from the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS) India, conducted during 2016-17.

pmc-11327252.title: Differential patch-leaving behavior during probabilistic foraging in humans and gerbils
pmc-11327252.creator: Lasse Güldener, Parthiban Saravanakumar, Max F K Happel, Frank W Ohl, Maike Vollmer, Stefan Pollmann
pmc-11327252.description: Foraging confronts animals, including humans, with the need to balance exploration and exploitation: exploiting a resource until it depletes and then deciding when to move to a new location for more resources. Research across various species has identified rules for when to leave a depleting patch, influenced by environmental factors like patch quality.

pmc-11459982.title: Pilot study for the development of an automatically generated and wearable-based early warning system for the detection of deterioration of hospitalized patients of an acute care hospital
pmc-11459982.creator: JJ Reichl, M Leifke, S Wehrli, D Kunz, L Geissmann, S Broisch, M Illien, D Wellauer, N von Dach, S Diener, V Manser, V Herren, A Angerer, S Hirsch, B Hölz, J Eckstein
pmc-11459982.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundAcute deteriorations of health status are common in hospitalized patients and are often preceded by changes in their vital signs. Events such as heart attacks, death or admission to the intensive care unit can be averted by early detection, therefore so-called Early Warning Scores (EWS) such as the National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2), including basic vital parameters such as heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature and level of consciousness, have been developed for a systematic approach.

pmc-11499986.title: Urbanization, loneliness and mental health model - A cross-sectional network analysis with a representative sample
pmc-11499986.creator: Dominika Ochnik, Bartłomiej Buława, Paulina Nagel, Marek Gachowski, Marcin Budziński
pmc-11499986.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). With increasing urbanization, more people are exposed to mental health risk factors stemming from the urban social or physical environment. However, research on the relationship between urbanization and mental health is lacking. This cross-sectional study aimed to explore the relationships of the physical environment (spatial cohesion and urban environment) and social factors (neighborhood cohesion) with mental health (stress, anxiety and depression symptoms) and physical health and the mediating role of loneliness based on the proposed theoretical model.

pmc-11514890.title: Sleep disturbance in patients with cirrhosis and transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt
pmc-11514890.creator: Ming Zhao, Yuling Yan, Xiaoze Wang, Bangxi Liu, Xuefeng Luo
pmc-11514890.description: BackgroundSleep disturbance (SD) is a common occurrence in individuals with cirrhosis and significantly impacts their quality of life. Datas regarding post transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) SD are scarce. This study aimed to explore the incidence and outcomes of post-TIPS SD.MethodsFrom August 2018 to November 2019, 73 patients who underwent TIPS were prospectively recruited for the study.

pmc-11710535.title: Linking Cognitive Function Index Item‐Level Responses to Tau Pathology in Amyloid Positive Cognitively Unimpaired individuals: Findings from The A4 Study
pmc-11710535.creator: Idris Demirsoy, Kellen K Petersen, Bhargav Teja Nallapu, Elham Ghanbarian, Richard B Lipton, Laura Rabin, Ali Ezzati
pmc-11710535.description: BackgroundThe Cognitive Function Index (CFI) is a validated test used to assess changes in self‐perceived cognitive and functional status as reported by an individual and their study partner. Previous studies have demonstrated an inverse correlation between higher amyloid‐beta (Aβ) burden and CFI, with certain CFI items exhibiting stronger associations than others.

pmc-12488406.title: Management of severe pneumonia in respiratory non-intensive care unit: a retrospective study from a single center experience
pmc-12488406.creator: Lucrezia Pisanu, Marianna Russo, Maria Arminio, Lorenzo Arlando, Valentina Conio, Francesco Rocco Bertuccio, Klodjana Mucaj, Mitela Tafa, Giulia Maria Stella, Angelo Guido Corsico
pmc-12488406.description: AimSevere pneumonia management in the hospital setting often relies heavily on established clinical practice and physician experience. This approach has the purpose of enabling early identification of risk factors most strongly associated with severe pneumonia at the time of hospital admission.

pmc-12496045.title: Health systems’ adaptations to climate change: an umbrella review of global evidence protocol
pmc-12496045.creator: Katarzyna Dubas‐Jakóbczyk, Nsikakabasi Samuel George, Costase Ndayishimiye
pmc-12496045.description: IntroductionHealth systems’ (HS) adaptations to climate change (CC) cover two major, and interrelated dimensions: (1) Environmental sustainability—actions aimed at limiting the negative impact of HS on the environment (eg, by reducing greenhouse gas emissions) and (2) Climate resilience—adaptations focused on improving HS’ ability to cope with the impact of CC (eg, by improving HS preparedness to climate-induced natural disasters).

pmc-12782610.title: Trait-Like and State-Like Oxytocin: A Biomarker of Alliance in Patients with Depression and Borderline Personality Disorder
pmc-12782610.creator: Galit Peysachov, Amit Tchizick, Jaime Delgadillo, Simone Shamay-Tsoory, Sigal Zilcha-Mano
pmc-12782610.description: IntroductionPatients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) show a poorer prognosis compared to patients without BPD. A potential contributor is the complexity of establishing a therapeutic alliance with patients with BPD. A potential underlying biological mechanism is oxytocin (OT), a hormone associated with social bonding and trust.

pmc-13001181.title: Strengthening and sustaining gender-based violence (GBV) coordination in emergencies: a synthesis of practitioner-driven, globally applicable recommendations
pmc-13001181.creator: Philomena Raftery, Alina Potts, Melanie Hyde, Yermeyn York Wuyke, Hira Hashmey, Liliane Munezero, Ligia Kiss, Mazeda Hossain, Jennifer Palmer
pmc-13001181.description: IntroductionGender-based violence (GBV) is a global public health and human rights crisis, requiring coordinated efforts to ensure effective prevention, risk mitigation, and response, particularly in emergencies. Despite policy commitments underlining the importance of addressing GBV in emergencies, funding remains insufficient, inconsistent, and poorly aligned with aid prioritisation in the changing humanitarian and global health financing landscape.

pmc-13077799.title: Percutaneous closure of residual leak after surgical left atrial appendage ligation: a case of stroke prevention in high-risk atrial fibrillation
pmc-13077799.creator: Mert Doğan, Ahmet Hakan Ateş, Cem Çöteli, Uğur Nadir Karakulak, Hikmet Yorgun, Mehmet Levent Sahiner, Ergun Barıs Kaya, Kudret Aytemir
pmc-13077799.description: Incomplete surgical left atrial appendage (LAA) closure is associated with increased thromboembolic risk in atrial fibrillation patients. We present a case of successful percutaneous closure of a significant residual leak following surgical LAA ligation. A 64-year-old female with atrial fibrillation (CHA₂DS₂-VASc score 4), prior surgical interventions including LAA ligation for thrombus formation, presented with ischemic stroke despite anticoagulation.

pmc-13149300.title: Activity of PROTAC MDM2 degrader in primary leukemia cells and PDX models
pmc-13149300.creator: Malathi Kandarpa, Luke F. Peterson, Harish Potu, Megha Ramappan, Yihong Liu, Avery Polk, Shaomeng Wang, Moshe Talpaz
pmc-13149300.description: MDM2 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes p53 tumor suppressor degradation and has emerged as a therapeutic target in the treatment of wild-type (wt) TP53 tumors. In acute myeloid leukemia (AML), TP53 mutations are infrequent (15–20%), but wt-p53 is often inactivated through overexpression of MDM2. Thus, MDM2 inhibitors are currently in clinical trials for AML.

pmc-13227518.title: Extra-large pore JZO zeolites with tunable Si/Al ratios as efficient catalysts for degradable plastic monomer production
pmc-13227518.creator: Shuman Gao, Xinxin Wang, Shaolei Gao, Mohammad Fahda, Dongyue Wang, Haijun Yu, Zijian You, Xiuning Liu, Liang Qi, Feng Shao, Peng Lu, Valentin Valtchev
pmc-13227518.description: JZO zeolite, the first stable aluminosilicate extra-large-pore zeolite, bridges the long-standing gap between microporous and mesoporous zeolites, offering highly accessible pore systems that are beneficial for molecular diffusion, active-site accessibility, and the processing of bulky molecules. However, the control of zeolite framework composition is limited, precluding its use in processes that require different acidic and ion-exchange properties.

pmc-13412505.title: Biopolymer-based nanoformulations accelerated tissue remodeling by antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and angiogenic potential
pmc-13412505.creator: Kunal Kishore, Saranga Rajesh, Sneha Sivadas, Nandakumar Selvasudha, R. Barathidasan, A. Hannah Rachel Vasanthi
pmc-13412505.description: OBJECTIVES:Designing a low-cost wound dressing material with better functionality enhances wound healing efficiently. Accordingly, a nanocomposite using pectin, keratin, ferulic acid, and silver nanoparticles exhibiting better wound healing potential was utilized to prepare gel and ointment to address inadequacies in wound management.

pmc-13421389.title: Optimization of milling operation parameters using Python-assisted GRA for enhanced surface quality and material behaviour
pmc-13421389.creator: Ganeshkumar Selvaraj, Ponni Ponnusamy, Ramakrishnan Thirumalaisamy, Manickaraj Karuppusamy, Jenyfal Sampson, Pravin Manikandan, Nivin Joy, Karthikayan Sundararajan, Kuwar Mausam, Sivasubramanian Palanisamy, Aravindhan Alagarsamy, Mezigebu Belay
pmc-13421389.description: Modern manufacturing's paradigm has changed a lot with the inclusion of optimization and smart manufacturing techniques. In this work, the performance of milling operation of magnesium alloy (Mg-AZ61) has been studied by using Box–Behnken Design (BBD) with Grey Relational Analysis (GRA). The main aim of this work is to optimize the operating parameters for better surface quality.

pmc-13520697.title: Lessons learned from the integration of virtual labs and at-home lab kits to enhance microbiology education during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13520697.creator: Beena G. Patel, John-Paul Vermitsky

pmc-13629202.title: From misdiagnosis to precision management: Thoracic vertebral infection caused by Scedosporium boydii diagnosed using a multi-platform approach — A case report and literature review
pmc-13629202.creator: Qihang Zou, Zhongjie He, Wenjie Fang, Hua Zhang, Daiwen Xiao
pmc-13629202.description: Scedosporium boydii spinal infection is rare and often mimics tuberculosis. We report a 54-year-old immunocompetent man with post-traumatic thoracic vertebral infection initially misdiagnosed as spinal tuberculosis. A multi-platform approach combining culture, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) identified S. boydii. Surgical debridement and voriconazole resulted in complete recovery.
